label: Hydraulic pressure
summary: Forklifts, car lifts, jacks, scissor lifts, tractors, log splitters and diggers use oil at very high pressure, often over 100 bar (1,500 psi). A pinhole leak can inject oil under the skin: it looks like a small prick but can cost a finger or a hand. Cutting a line or opening a valve can drop a raised load instantly.
signs: Rubber hoses with crimped steel fittings running to rams and cylinders
Oily film, drips or puddles around hoses and joints
Raised forks, buckets, platforms or tipper beds
Round or cylinder-shaped accumulator tanks on bigger machines
A fine mist or jet of oil from a fitting
do: Lower every load to the ground or onto solid blocks before working
Turn the engine off and work the controls to release pressure
Look for leaks with a piece of cardboard or wood, never your hand
Block raised parts with stands or timber; don't rely on the hydraulics
Let hot oil cool before opening anything
dont: Don't run a hand or finger along a hose to find a leak
Don't loosen fittings on a system under pressure
Don't stand or reach under a load held up only by hydraulics
Don't cut hoses on a machine with anything raised
Don't open, drill or cut an accumulator tank or its fittings: it stays charged with gas and oil pressure after the engine stops
ppe: Safety glasses, with a face shield over them
Thick gloves (they won’t stop an oil jet)
firstAid: Any oil injection injury is an emergency even if it looks tiny: it needs a surgeon within hours
Keep the injured part still and level; don't squeeze it or wrap it tightly
Hot oil burns: cool under cool running water for 20 minutes
Oil in an eye: rinse with clean water for at least 15 minutes
